question.text:
CASE STUDY (continued): Mrs. Lakshmi's KYC was done 8 years ago with her old school address. She has moved to a new residence and her Aadhaar is not linked to her mutual fund accounts.
Question 2: What is the correct sequence of actions Mrs. Lakshmi should take to update her KYC and link Aadhaar?

answer.text: Only update Aadhaar on the UIDAI website and the mutual fund records will auto-update
File a new KYC application as her old KYC is invalid after 8 years
Submit a KRA/CKYC change form with address proof (and Aadhaar number / e-KYC where applicable); the KRA updates the mutual funds; update only folio-specific non-KYC details directly with the AMC/RTA
No action needed — KYC is a one-time process and never needs updating

explanation.text: The Logic: KYC records (including address) are held centrally by the KRA/CKYC system. To change the address, Mrs. Lakshmi submits a KRA/CKYC change form with valid address proof (and provides her Aadhaar number / e-KYC where applicable). The KRA then communicates the updated KYC information to the mutual funds, so the address need not be changed folio by folio. Only folio-specific, non-KYC details (such as bank account details, mode of holding, or nomination) are updated directly with each AMC/RTA. The Trap: KYC registration is "one-time," but KYC details must be UPDATED when they change. Updating Aadhaar with UIDAI does not by itself flow into the KYC records, and a brand-new KYC is not required just because the existing one is several years old. Note: Folio-specific changes such as bank details, mode of holding and nomination are processed by the AMC/RTA for each folio, not via the KRA.
